clue.text: Mark's sweet !

definitions.meaning: the centre of a target, the spot an archer or darts player aims for
a hard, striped peppermint-flavoured boiled sweet popular in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: The same term names both the central ring of a dartboard target and a striped British boiled confection, so each clue word is one sense.

clue.text: Frail nautical casks ?.

parts.note: small water barrels carried on boats share their name with things that break easily, as fragile objects do

explanation.surface: Barrels on a ship that are flimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: A breaker is a small keg carried in a ship's boat; 'frail' points at things that break.
explanation.definitionFit: On ships a breaker is a small cask for drinking water, and the word literally means things that break, as fragile items do.

clue.text: Teach girl appearing unusually torpid

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of teach girl appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A teacher's pupil seems strangely sluggish in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges TEACH GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic and torpid both mean sluggish and lacking energy; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Large, number in some battle

indicators.note: the letter for a large number is put inside the word some

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: A great many fell in a certain battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of the Somme (1916) was a First World War battle in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is the river in France that gave its name to a huge 1916 battle.

clue.text: Americans look for no recession

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: to seek is to look for
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: US citizens are hoping the economy will not slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks economic; it reverses SEEKNAY in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is an informal name for people from the United States.

clue.text: Dexterous little publicity trio is replaced

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a little piece of publicity

indicators.note: the letters of the word trio are put back in a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small advertising team of three gets swapped out for a more skilful one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is replaced' rearranges TRIO into ROIT, which follows AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone skilful and nimble with hands or mind; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Went round about refusal to give up explosive

indicators.note: in a down clue, giving up means going upwards, so the letters are read from bottom to top
the word for went round goes about the word for refusal, enclosing it

parts.note: rotated means turned or went round
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Someone circled and refused to surrender a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NO inside ROTATED, giving ROTANOTED; 'to give up' reverses that, since the clue reads downwards. A detonator is the device that sets off an explosive charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is an explosive device used to set off a larger charge.

clue.text: All right — a sanctimonious beast !

parts.note: OK means all right
pi is informal British slang for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a self-righteous animal.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is British slang for self-righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African forest animal related to the giraffe, an example of a beast.

clue.text: Informative bank man ?

parts.note: the person at a bank counter who counts out money also, by the literal sense, is one who tells or recounts things

explanation.surface: A banker who gives out useful information.
explanation.walkthrough: A bank cashier has this title; read literally it is one who tells, so 'informative'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank cashier is called this, and literally the word means one who tells.

clue.text: Russian leader makes mark when about fifty

indicators.note: the word for mark goes about the numeral, wrapping around it

parts.note: a stain is a mark
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A Soviet chief scores a mark when he reaches his fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside STAIN; 'makes' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin led the Soviet Union from the 1920s until 1953.

clue.text: Site meant to be adapted for a café

indicators.note: something adapted is altered into a new form, so the letters of site meant are reworked

explanation.surface: A building plot is earmarked for conversion into a little coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be adapted' rearranges SITE MEANT. The word is French, for a small bar or café selling drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or bistro, a kind of modest café.

clue.text: Path appears right in the end

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the word for the end

parts.note: a tail is the end of something, as in the tail of a procession

explanation.surface: A footpath seems to come out correct at its final stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a track or rough path through countryside, a synonym.

clue.text: Deceitful person might get cut?

parts.note: the rogue word is also the jack in a pack of cards, and a pack is cut before dealing, so this card might turn up at the cut

explanation.surface: A liar could end up being snubbed or wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' seems to mean snubbed or injured; it is cutting a pack of cards, where this card (the jack) can be shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest rogue, and the same word names the jack in playing cards.

clue.text: For instance, a linnet ruined the wild rose

parts.note: EG, from Latin exempli gratia, means for instance

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its shape, so the letters of a linnet are scrambled

explanation.surface: A songbird, say, has trampled a hedgerow bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns A LINNET into LANTINE, after EG. A linnet is a small songbird, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the old name for sweetbriar, a wild rose of hedgerows.

clue.text: The right grades are changed in these respects

indicators.note: the letters of grades are changed into a different order

explanation.surface: Marks awarded are revised, and a teacher says the right ones apply in certain matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are changed' turns GRADES into EGARDS, after R. 'in these' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Regards and respects are both plural nouns for aspects or particulars, as in 'in all respects'.

clue.text: An outstanding plan?

parts.note: outstanding is read as standing out, raised up; a plan is a map, so this chart has a raised surface

explanation.surface: An excellent scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise; it means literally standing out, as hills do on a raised chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A map that shows hills and valleys in raised form, or by shading, is a chart of the land's ups and downs.

clue.text: Warning to go on board?

parts.note: a formal warning can be pinned up on the board in a hallway that carries announcements, as if told to board a ship

explanation.surface: An instruction to embark on a ship or plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go on board' suggests boarding a vessel; it means being pinned to a noticeboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone notice is warning them in advance, and an announcement pinned to a board carries the same name.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman takes vehicle to go abroad, nothing more

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a vehicle
aller is French for to go, so it is to go in a foreign language
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A Spanish gent hails a taxi to travel overseas, and that is all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells you to use a foreign word: the French 'aller'. 'more' joins the O on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is the Spanish word for a gentleman or knight.

clue.text: Envy possession of new drug-ask East about it

indicators.note: the words for ask and East go about the anagram, around it

parts.note: to beg is to ask
E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: new signals a new arrangement of the letters of drug

explanation.surface: Someone resents another having a new narcotic, and asks an eastern contact about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DRUG into RUDG; 'about' puts that inside BEG plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to resent someone having something, so to envy them.

clue.text: Lots of notes on fish

definitions.meaning: series of musical tones running up and down an octave
the small overlapping plates covering a fish's skin

explanation.definitionFit: The plural word covers ascending sequences of musical tones practised by pianists and the protective plates on the body of a trout or carp.

clue.text: She's on the right lines, providing wine

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A woman is travelling correctly by rail, offering a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway) is a crossword convention for 'lines'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain.

clue.text: Story of ARP organization taken to island retreat

indicators.note: organizing letters means arranging them afresh, so ARP is rearranged
retreating means going backwards, so the island's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: An account of the wartime air-raid wardens' group withdrawing to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization' turns ARP into PAR; 'retreat' turns ELBA into ABLE. ARP was Air Raid Precautions, Britain's wartime civil defence service.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral tale, a kind of story.

clue.text: Carriage way between two rivers

indicators.note: the abbreviation for way goes between the names of the rivers

parts.note: the Po is the main river of northern Italy
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A coach road runs between a pair of rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' looks like a coach; it means bearing, how you hold yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage can mean the way a person holds their body, which is posture.

clue.text: Raising problem in a spirit of hostility?

indicators.note: raising in a down clue lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Bringing up an issue in a hostile mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' reverses the whole run SUM + IN + A, giving ANIMUS. 'in' and 'a' are both taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is hostile feeling or ill will toward someone.

clue.text: Little Oliver East knows a sculptor

parts.note: Noll is a pet form of the name Oliver, famously used of Oliver Cromwell
E is the compass abbreviation for east
to ken is Scottish and old English for to know, so kens means knows

explanation.surface: A small boy called Oliver from the east of England is acquainted with an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Nollekens (1737–1823) was a London sculptor of portrait busts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nollekens was an eighteenth-century English artist known for his marble busts, so he is an example of a sculptor.

clue.text: Miss Bennet's confounded daily

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters of daily are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Jane Austen heroine's cleaning lady is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' rearranges DAILY. In Britain a 'daily' is a cleaner who comes in each day. In Pride and Prejudice, Lydia is the youngest Bennet sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is the youngest of the Bennet sisters in Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Happy-looking chap, but a non-starter, this runner

indicators.note: a non-starter here means the word loses its starting letter

parts.note: a smiler is someone who looks happy

explanation.surface: A cheerful man turns out to be no use as an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a non-starter' sounds like a failure; it removes the S that starts SMILER.
explanation.definitionFit: A miler is an athlete who races over the distance of one mile.

clue.text: Fly with obscure climber, middle-aged

indicators.note: in a down clue a climber goes upwards, so the word for obscure is read bottom to top

parts.note: dim means obscure or faint

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word aged are taken

explanation.surface: An insect with a little-known climbing plant, getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' looks like a plant; it reverses DIM to MID. 'middle-aged' takes GE, the middle of AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny two-winged fly that swarms near water.

clue.text: She's returned by herself

indicators.note: read backwards the word gives back exactly itself, so it is its own reversal

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A woman is elected again without any help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' looks like a vote count; it means reversed, and the word reversed is the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a woman, so it stands for 'she'.

clue.text: Shot principal Parliamentarian

parts.note: a round is a single shot fired from a gun
the head of a school is its principal

explanation.surface: A leading member of Parliament was gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: In the English Civil War (1642–51), a Roundhead was a supporter of Parliament against King Charles I, named after the short haircuts of Puritans.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundheads were the soldiers and supporters of the Parliament side in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Notes from an instrument on board

definitions.text: Notes from an instrument on board

parts.words: Notes from an instrument on board
parts.note: the raised black keys of a piano keyboard play semitones written with a hash-like sign, and cheats working a card table are also so named

explanation.surface: Music played on deck by a ship's band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship; it is the keyboard, where the black keys give these raised notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp is a note raised a semitone, as played on the black keys of a piano.

clue.text: This girl might appear short of coin

definitions.text: This girl might appear short of coin

parts.words: This girl might appear short of coin
parts.note: the girl's name is shortened to Penny, which is also a coin, so she seems short of money

explanation.surface: A young woman looks as if she is out of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of coin' seems to mean hard up; it says her short name is a coin's name, Penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope is a girl's name whose usual pet form is Penny, the British small coin.
